intent:
"yes approbe and begin the implementation" started the bstack build slice by slice, strictly one at a time ("keep it sequential"). Later: "i'm only not concerned about security hardening, threat-model concerns. Style and simplification and following proper design principles are still important." - build the full app fast, but review the core properly so slices and phases do not leave bugs.

The plans of record are in the repo: `docs/design.md` (requirements and decisions, including R24: licensing is out of scope) and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (tasks, task evidence contract). knowttl/bstack is public, has no GitHub Actions or workflows and no release automation, and ships through the no-mistakes pipeline (`.no-mistakes.yaml` owns the review budget and focus) with automatic merge of green work. Phase 0 and task T1.1 (fixtures, last in https://github.com/knowttl/bstack/pull/13) have landed. The merged slice table is `/home/brytton/.treehouse/firstmate-5911dd/3/firstmate/data/slice-merge/report.md` (bstack table).

This piece is slice C7a, the first part of task T1.2 "Build the evaluation runner and record the baseline": the acceptance registry and the manual evaluation interface (slice done evidence: 75 owned case IDs, invalid registry and manual results blocked, explicit transcript scoring). C7b follows with the current-host adapter, isolation and the recorded baseline.
amendments: C7a supplies the registry, scenarios and manual scoring interface. T1.2 remains incomplete until C7b supplies the adapter, verified isolation and actual comparable baseline runs.
Evidence-only commit follows the tested implementation commit.
C7b first refresh: reran the C7a command set against the landed C7a commit, including owner assignment, table-driven completed-procedure matching and baseline comparison checks.
